# The Growth Den

> The Growth Den is Logan Ice's fractional growth advisory, founded in 2025 and based in St. Louis, Missouri. Logan is a growth advisor for growth-stage DTC and e-commerce brands ($5M to $80M in revenue) who handles strategy and takes execution off your plate: the same senior person decides where the next marketing dollar goes and then does the work alongside the client's team. He plugs in wherever growth is stuck: as head of growth, head of creative, a hands-on Meta media buyer alongside an existing growth lead, building the marketing team and its systems, or as an interim head of marketing between leaders. Engagements start at $7,500 per month whichever seat he's in, scoped up from there by how many services he covers and how much building is involved. Clients get a weekly leadership session, same-day replies, and systems their team keeps. Larger go-to-market programs are scoped separately.

How he works: every business is judged on MER (total revenue over total marketing cost) and contribution margin, with a break-even MER derived from margin and a target set above it. The first 90 days are written as a list of bets, each with a cost, a success measure and a stop date. Ad creative comes from a repeatable loop (name the default angle, force genuinely different angles away from it, test them on independent customer personas, then produce). Everything built (the scorecard, the creative loop, launch tooling, SOPs, training) lives in the client's accounts and name, so the team owns the system when the engagement ends.

Logan's background: founder and fractional growth advisor at The Growth Den, St. Louis, Missouri. Growth roles at P&G, Varsity Tutors (Series A through C, three cities to an international brand; it later IPO'd at $1.4B), Slalom, Little Passports, Wuffes (grew from $14M to $40M+) and Equifax. BA in Physics and Psychology from Washington University in St. Louis. He builds simple AI tools (creative pipelines, reporting dashboards, launch workflows, incrementality checks) into how client teams work, and teaches the teams to run them. He judges marketing on MER and contribution margin across the whole business rather than any one platform's attribution.

Contact: logan@thegrowthden.com · Book a call: https://calendar.app.google/dy8683mNDXyWAkPo9

## Services
- [What a fractional head of growth actually does for a DTC brand](https://thegrowthden.com/fractional-head-of-growth/): A fractional head of growth owns your acquisition and retention numbers part-time and, unlike most fractional CMOs, does the work rather than just directing it. I'm Logan Ice. For growth-stage DTC and e-commerce brands doing roughly $5M to $80M, this is the seat I fill most often. I decide with you where the next marketing dollar goes, then help make it happen, from $7,500 a month.
- [A fractional head of creative for DTC and e-commerce ads](https://thegrowthden.com/fractional-head-of-creative/): If your ads look like everyone else's and your team can't produce new angles fast enough, you need a fractional head of creative who can also run the production. I'm Logan Ice. In this seat I build a creative engine that finds genuinely different angles, tests them before they go live, and turns the winners into finished ads quickly with AI. It starts at $7,500 a month.
- [A Meta media buyer who also brings strategy](https://thegrowthden.com/meta-media-buyer/): If you already have a growth lead and what you're missing is someone great inside Meta Ads Manager, this is the service for you. I'm Logan Ice. I buy media hands-on, restructure accounts around how the algorithm works today, and build the tooling that makes launching and reading results fast. Because I also think like a strategist, your growth lead gets a partner, not just a pair of hands. It starts at $7,500 a month.
- [Help building a marketing team and its systems](https://thegrowthden.com/marketing-team-builder/): If you're about to hire your first or next marketer, or your team has grown faster than its processes, I plug in to design the team and build the systems they'll run. I'm Logan Ice. I've built and led growth teams at companies from startups to Equifax, and I build the AI workflows and SOPs your team keeps. It starts at $7,500 a month.
- [An interim head of marketing, or CMO, for the gap between leaders](https://thegrowthden.com/interim-head-of-marketing/): When your marketing leader leaves, goes on leave, or hasn't been hired yet, the team and the budget still need an owner on Monday. I step into the seat for a fixed window, usually three to six months, run the team and the number, and help you hire and hand over to the permanent person. I'm Logan Ice. Like every service here, it starts at $7,500 a month and is scoped to the size of the job.

## Straight answers
- [Agency, in-house hire, or fractional growth lead: what actually changes at $5M to $80M](https://thegrowthden.com/agency-vs-fractional/): An agency is paid to keep your account and grow your spend. An in-house hire is paid to be there. A fractional growth lead is paid to build something you own and make the number move. Here is what each one is structurally good and bad at, without the sales pitch, from someone who has been on all three sides.
- [How to set a MER target from your contribution margin, and hold whoever runs your ads to it](https://thegrowthden.com/mer-target/): Break-even MER is one divided by your contribution margin before marketing. If your margin is 30%, a 3.33x MER means you made nothing. Most "what's a good MER" advice skips that math, which is why brands celebrate numbers that are losing them money. Here is the math, a calculator, and how I use it as the accountability contract for whoever runs your ads.
- [When a DTC brand should hire a fractional growth lead, and when it shouldn't](https://thegrowthden.com/when-to-hire/): The right time is usually earlier than founders think and later than agencies say. Roughly $5M to $80M in revenue, a real marketing budget with no senior owner, and one of a handful of moments that reshuffle the whole growth system. Here are the signs it's time, the situations where I'd tell you not to, and a quick self-check.
- [Twelve questions that tell you whether a fractional CMO builds or just advises](https://thegrowthden.com/how-to-evaluate-a-fractional-cmo/): Plenty of fractional marketing leaders are strategy-only, and most interview guides won't catch that until month three. These are the questions I'd ask if I were hiring someone like me, including the two that most candidates can't answer: show me the last ad account you personally ran, and how do you plan to make yourself unnecessary.
- [A consultant who trains your marketing team to use AI for creative and reporting, then leaves them running it](https://thegrowthden.com/ai-training-for-marketing-teams/): Most AI training for marketers is a workshop about prompts. Your team goes back to their desks and nothing changes. What I do is different. I look at how your team actually produces ads and reports today, build the AI workflows into those jobs with them, and coach them until they can run and extend the workflows without me. I'm Logan Ice. Here is what that looks like, who it's for, and what it costs.
- [How do I build a marketing system my team owns instead of relying on an agency?](https://thegrowthden.com/marketing-system-you-own/): You already know the feeling. The agency has the accounts, the reporting and the know-how, and if they left tomorrow you'd be starting over. Building a system your team owns doesn't mean firing them. It means five things live in your house, in your name, run by your people: the scorecard, the creative loop, the launch tooling, the SOPs, and the training. Here is how I build that with clients, and how to start without me.
- [A fractional growth advisor for DTC and e-commerce brands, based in St. Louis](https://thegrowthden.com/st-louis/): I'm Logan Ice, a fractional growth advisor who lives and works in St. Louis. Most of my clients aren't here, and that's fine. The ones who are get something the remote ones don't, which is a working session at the same table. If you're a Missouri or Midwest brand looking for someone who does strategy and Meta execution and isn't an agency, this page is for you.

## Notes from the Den
- [How to earn trust](https://thegrowthden.com/notes/how-to-earn-trust/) (2026-10-01): Logan Ice on the simplest advice he has for anyone at any stage of their career: be useful before you're asked, do what you said you would do, and tell people the truth early. Less about marketing this week, more about being a good person to work with.
- [Using the Right Lure](https://thegrowthden.com/notes/using-the-right-lure/) (2026-09-26): A stranger found Logan Ice through ChatGPT because his website says one specific thing about how he works. Why a narrow, plain-spoken pitch helps you get found now that buyers ask AI for help, and what to change on your own site this week.
- [Dungeons & Dragons & Dialogue, Six Years Later](https://thegrowthden.com/notes/dnd-dialogue-six-years-later/) (2026-09-15): Six years after writing about how D&D makes you better at your job, Logan Ice revisits empathy, diversity and ambiguity from the Dungeon Master's side of the table, adds what changes when AI agents join the party, and makes the case for a Session Zero in every client engagement.
- [The Angle Storm Pack](https://thegrowthden.com/notes/angle-storm-pack/) (2026-09-10): Logan Ice's creative development loop for paid social as seven prompts you can paste into Claude or ChatGPT: name the default angle, force new angles away from it, score them, test them on five independent personas, and loop until one of them fights for an angle.
